meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'kind', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'morning', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

meanings.note: 'Проходите!' = Come in! (inviting a guest)
Secondary conversational sense ('to pass, to go through') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to finish', forming an aspectual pair with 'заканчивать'.

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'уйти'.

examples.text: Уходи отсюда скорее, пока шеф не увидел тебя без формы!
examples.trans: Get out of here quickly before the chef sees you without a uniform!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('job') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to excuse, to forgive') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: + на: опоздать на работу = be late for work
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Я прекрасно понимаю = I understand perfectly
Secondary conversational sense ('wonderful!') (as a reply) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нет, лучше так: все говорят, а я делаю! Прекрасно.
examples.trans: No, better like this: everyone talks, while I do! Excellent.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: to stay longer than intended or be late

examples.trans: I will be delayed at work.
I will also be delayed a bit today.

examples.text: А я шеф, я немного задержусь!
examples.trans: And I am the chef, I will be a little late!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'вести'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to spend', forming an aspectual pair with 'проводить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to lead, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We spent the evening at home.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, to go out

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встретиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to meet up') (+ с + instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've been dating for a month.
We've been going out for a month already.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian name meaning 'Maxim', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Максим, я внимательно прочла ваше резюме.
examples.trans: Maksim, I carefully read your résumé.
Maxim, where are you getting ready to go now?

examples.text: Я хотела отомстить Максиму через тебя.
examples.trans: I wanted to revenge on Maxim through you.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'давать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to ask'.

examples.text: Все ваши вопросы задавайте в мэрию!
examples.trans: Address all your questions to the mayor's office!

examples.text: Не задавай глупых вопросов, работай быстрее!
examples.trans: Do not ask stupid questions, work faster!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

молчать.gloss: to be silent, to say nothing

meanings.en: to be silent, to keep quiet
meanings.note: почему ты молчишь? = why aren't you saying anything?

examples.text: Ну что ты молчишь? Ты толстый, ты не спортсмен!
examples.trans: Well, why are you so quiet? You're fat, you're no athlete!

examples.text: Молчи лучше, пока шеф не заметил нашу ошибку!
examples.trans: Better keep quiet before the chef notices our mistake!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: + dative of the person: обещать вам

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
